Binghamton Police prepares multi-layered LUMA festival security plan

By Jolie Jenkins
Published: Sep. 8, 2026 at 3:46 PM EDT|Updated: 12 hours ago
Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:55
Instaread

BINGHAMTON, N.Y. (WBNG) -- As downtown Binghamton transforms for the LUMA Projection Arts Festival from Sept. 11-12, preparations are moving forward on a precise construction schedule.

To ensure a safe atmosphere for the estimated 30,000 attendees, the Binghamton Police Department (BPD) is planning for a strong security presence throughout the festival outline.

“Don’t stray on your own. It is a large crowd, so make sure you’re keeping track of those in your group, especially young children,” said BPD’s Lieutenant Dan Keller.

Keller announced that officers will utilize bicycle patrols, plainclothes personnel, drones and downtown surveillance cameras to monitor the crowds.

“So inside of the Luma footprint, there is no waiver of the open container law, so you have to be on private property to consume alcohol. So, either in one of the establishments or on somebody’s residence. Streets, sidewalks, no open containers are going to be permitted,” Keller said.

Authorities also advise those planning to drink to behave responsibly and establish a clear transportation plan to get home safely.

Because streetlights are turned off inside the festival boundaries to enhance the projection displays, Keller suggests that anyone with difficulty seeing in the dark carry a small flashlight.

“I would say that it is dark downtown. We shut the streetlights off inside of the Luma footprint so that you can see the beautiful projections,” Keller said.

Parents are also strongly urged to keep a close eye on their children in the dense crowds and immediately contact an officer if a child becomes separated.

“If your child steps away for a minute, it may be tricky to find them. If that happens, I’d recommend that you come find one of the many police officers and we will reunite you,” Keller said.

To accommodate the extensive setup and staging equipment, multiple Downtown Binghamton streets will close to traffic beginning Tuesday night:

From Sept. 8 at 7 p.m. to Sept. 9 at 4 a.m.

  • Court Street between Washington Street and State Street
  • Exchange Street between Hawley Street and Court Street
  • Hawley Street between Isbell Street and Exchange Street

From Sept. 9 at 7 p.m. to Sept. 10 at 4 a.m.

  • Court Street between Water Street and Washington Street
  • Chenango Street between Court Street and Henry Street
  • Exchange Street right turn onto Court Street

From Sept. 10 at 7 p.m. to Sept. 13 at 3 a.m.

  • Court Street between Water Street and Carroll Street
  • Washington Street between the entrance to the parking garage and Court Street
  • State Street between Hawley Street and Commercial Alley
  • Collier Street between the entrance to the Collier Street Parking Lot and Court Street
  • Chenango Street between Court Street and Henry Street
  • Exchange Street between Hawley Street and Court Street
  • Hawley Street between Collier Street and Exchange Street
  • All of Congdon Place
